title: Checking in
settingKo: 호텔 프런트에서 체크인을 합니다.

lines.text: Good evening. Do you have a reservation?
Yes, I booked a room for two nights under Lee.
Here it is. Could I see your passport, please?
lines.ko: 여기 있네요. 여권 좀 볼 수 있을까요?

lines.text: Of course. What time is breakfast?
It's from seven to ten in the main restaurant.

phrases.en: I booked a room for two nights.
What time is breakfast?

response.situationKo: 호텔 직원이 방에 문제가 없었는지 묻습니다. 에어컨이 고장 났다고 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: How is your room? Is everything okay?

answers.text: Actually, the air conditioner isn't working.
answers.noteKo: Actually로 시작하면 문제를 부드럽게 꺼낼 수 있어요.

answers.text: It's nice, but the AC is broken. Could someone check it?
I'm sorry to bother you, but the air conditioning doesn't seem to work.
The air con's not working, I'm afraid.

title: Weekend plans
settingKo: 금요일 오후, 친구와 주말 계획을 이야기합니다.

lines.text: Do you have any plans for the weekend?
Not really. I might just stay home and rest.
Some of us are going hiking on Saturday. Want to come?
lines.ko: 우리 몇 명이 토요일에 등산 가는데. 같이 갈래?

lines.text: That sounds fun! What time are you leaving?
Around eight. I can pick you up.

gist.questionKo: 두 사람은 토요일에 무엇을 할 가능성이 큰가요?

phrases.en: Do you have any plans for the weekend?
That sounds fun!

response.situationKo: 친구가 저녁 식사에 초대합니다. 수락하거나 정중히 거절해 보세요.
response.prompt: We're having dinner at my place on Friday. Can you make it?

answers.text: Sure, I'd love to! What time should I come?
Sorry, I can't make it on Friday. Maybe next time?
That's very kind of you, but I already have plans.
Sounds great! Should I bring anything?

title: Returning a shirt
settingKo: 옷가게에 산 셔츠를 가져가 교환을 요청합니다.

lines.text: Hi. I bought this shirt yesterday, but it's too small.
lines.ko: 안녕하세요. 어제 이 셔츠를 샀는데 너무 작아요.

lines.text: No problem. Do you have your receipt?
Yes, here you are. Can I exchange it for a large?
lines.ko: 네, 여기요. 라지로 교환할 수 있나요?

lines.text: Let me check. I'm sorry, we only have it in blue now.
lines.ko: 확인해 볼게요. 죄송하지만 지금은 파란색만 있어요.

lines.text: Blue is fine. Thanks for your help.

phrases.en: It's too small.
Can I exchange it for a large?

response.situationKo: 온라인으로 산 물건이 망가진 채 왔습니다. 고객센터 직원에게 환불을 요청해 보세요.
response.prompt: Thanks for calling. How can I help you today?

answers.text: Hi, the item I ordered arrived broken. Can I get a refund?
answers.noteKo: 문제와 원하는 것을 한 번에 말했어요.

answers.text: I'd like to return this because it was damaged.
My order came broken. I want my money back.
answers.noteKo: 직접적이어서 상황에 따라 강하게 들릴 수 있어요.

answers.text: I'm calling about a damaged item. What should I do?
answers.noteKo: I'm calling about은 전화 첫 문장으로 좋아요.

title: Looking at an apartment
settingKo: 월세 집을 보러 가서 집주인에게 조건을 묻습니다.

lines.text: So this is the living room. It gets a lot of sun.
It's really nice. How much is the rent?
It's nine hundred a month, and the internet is included.
Are pets allowed? I have a small cat.
lines.ko: 반려동물 키워도 되나요? 작은 고양이가 있어요.

lines.text: A cat is fine, but no dogs, sorry.
lines.ko: 고양이는 괜찮은데 개는 안 돼요, 죄송해요.

phrases.en: How much is the rent?
Are pets allowed?

response.situationKo: 집주인이 궁금한 게 있는지 묻습니다. 조건 하나를 물어보세요.
response.prompt: Do you have any other questions about the place?

answers.text: Yes, are utilities included in the rent?
When can I move in?
Could you tell me how much the deposit is?
Just one. Is there a washing machine?
answers.noteKo: Just one으로 질문을 하나만 한다고 알려요.

title: Where's my package?
settingKo: 온라인으로 산 물건이 오지 않아 고객센터에 연락합니다.

lines.text: Hi, thanks for calling. How can I help you today?
lines.ko: 안녕하세요, 전화 주셔서 감사합니다. 무엇을 도와드릴까요?

lines.text: My package says delivered, but I didn't get it.
lines.ko: 배송 완료라고 나오는데 저는 못 받았어요.

lines.text: I'm sorry about that. Can I have your order number?
Sure, it's four five two eight nine.
Thanks. We'll send a new one tomorrow.

phrases.en: My package says delivered, but I didn't get it.
Can I have your order number?

response.situationKo: 주문한 물건이 망가져서 왔어요. 고객센터에 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Hello, what seems to be the problem?

answers.text: My order arrived broken. Can I get a refund?
Hi, the item I got is damaged. Could you replace it, please?
Hey, my headphones came broken. What can I do?
The box was damaged and the cup inside is broken.

title: I'm allergic to nuts
settingKo: 식당에서 주문하면서 알레르기를 알립니다.

lines.text: Are you ready to order, or do you need a minute?
I'm ready. Does the salad have any nuts in it?
Yes, it comes with walnuts. Are you allergic?
Yes. Can I have it without the walnuts?
lines.ko: 네. 호두 빼고 주실 수 있나요?

lines.text: No problem. I'll tell the kitchen.

phrases.en: Does it have any nuts in it?
Can I have it without the walnuts?

response.situationKo: 직원이 못 먹는 음식이 있는지 묻습니다. 대답해 보세요.
response.prompt: Do you have any food allergies we should know about?

answers.text: Yes, I'm allergic to shrimp.
No, I can eat everything. Thanks for asking.
I don't eat meat. I'm vegetarian.
Just no peanuts for me, please. I have an allergy.
answers.noteKo: no + 음식 + for me로 간단히 말해요.

title: My tooth hurts
settingKo: 치과에서 아픈 이를 설명합니다.

lines.text: So, what brings you in today?
My back tooth hurts when I drink something cold.
How long has it been hurting?
About a week. It's getting worse.
OK, let's take an X-ray first.

phrases.en: My tooth hurts when I drink something cold.
It's getting worse.

response.situationKo: 의사가 얼마나 아픈지 묻습니다. 대답해 보세요.
response.prompt: On a scale of one to ten, how bad is the pain?

answers.text: Maybe a seven. It's pretty bad.
About a five. It's not too bad.
I'd say it's around an eight, especially at night.
Honestly, a nine! It really hurts.

title: The train is delayed
settingKo: 기차가 늦어져서 역무원에게 묻습니다.

lines.text: Excuse me, is the train to Boston delayed?
Yes, it's about forty minutes late because of the snow.
Oh no. I have a meeting at two.
There's a bus at twelve thirty. It might be faster.
lines.ko: 12시 30분에 버스가 있어요. 그게 더 빠를 수도 있어요.

phrases.en: Is the train delayed?
It might be faster.

response.situationKo: 친구에게 기차가 늦어서 약속에 늦는다고 문자로 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Hey, are you still coming at three?

answers.text: Sorry, my train is delayed. I'll be thirty minutes late.
Yes, but I'm running a bit late. The train is slow.
I'm so sorry, the train has been delayed. Could we meet at three thirty instead?
Ugh, train's delayed! See you around three thirty?

title: Renting a car
settingKo: 여행지에서 차를 빌립니다.

lines.text: Hi, do you have a reservation with us?
Yes, a small car for three days.
Great. Do you want full insurance? It's fifteen dollars a day.
Yes, please. And do I need to return it with a full tank?
lines.ko: 네, 그걸로요. 그리고 기름을 가득 채워서 반납해야 하나요?

lines.text: Yes, or we charge you for the gas.

gist.questionKo: 차를 반납할 때 해야 할 것은?

phrases.en: Do I need to return it with a full tank?
A small car for three days.

response.situationKo: 직원이 차를 어디서 반납할지 묻습니다.
response.prompt: Will you return the car here, or at the airport?

answers.text: I'll return it here, on Friday.
Can I return it at the airport?
At the airport, please, if that's possible.
The airport works better for me.
answers.noteKo: works better for me는 '저한테 더 편해요'예요.

title: Messaging the host
settingKo: 숙소 호스트에게 체크인 방법을 묻습니다.

lines.text: Hi, we're arriving around ten tonight. Is that OK?
No problem. It's self check-in.
The key is in a lock box. The code is two four six one.
Perfect. Where can we park the car?
There's free parking behind the building.

phrases.en: We're arriving around ten tonight.
Where can we park the car?

response.situationKo: 호스트가 숙소에 필요한 게 있는지 묻습니다. 하나 부탁해 보세요.
response.prompt: Is there anything else you need for your stay?

answers.text: Could we have some extra towels, please?
Can we check out a little late on Sunday?
No, we're all good. Thanks!
Is there a hair dryer? I can't find one.
answers.noteKo: can't find one으로 못 찾았다고 말해요.

title: I lost my phone
settingKo: 카페에 두고 온 휴대폰을 찾으러 갑니다.

lines.text: Hi, I think I left my phone here about an hour ago.
lines.ko: 안녕하세요, 한 시간쯤 전에 여기 휴대폰을 두고 간 것 같아요.

lines.text: What does it look like?
It's black with a green case.
Is this it? Someone found it on the table.
Yes! Thank you so much. I was so worried.

phrases.en: I think I left my phone here.
phrases.ko: 여기 휴대폰을 두고 간 것 같아요.

phrases.en: It's black with a green case.

response.situationKo: 분실물 센터 직원이 무엇을 잃어버렸는지 묻습니다.
response.prompt: What did you lose, and where?

answers.text: I lost my wallet on the subway this morning.
I left my backpack at the bus stop. It's blue.
I'm afraid I lost my laptop bag somewhere in the station.
answers.noteKo: I'm afraid는 안 좋은 소식을 말할 때 써요.

answers.text: My AirPods! I think I left them on the train.

title: My card isn't working
settingKo: 해외에서 카드가 결제되지 않아 은행에 전화합니다.

lines.text: Hi, my card isn't working. I'm traveling in Japan.
lines.ko: 안녕하세요, 카드가 안 돼요. 일본 여행 중이에요.

lines.text: I see. For security, we blocked it. Did you buy something big?
lines.ko: 그렇군요. 보안 때문에 정지됐어요. 큰 금액을 결제하셨나요?

lines.text: Yes, I paid for a hotel yesterday.
OK, I unblocked it. You can use it now.
lines.ko: 네, 정지를 풀었어요. 이제 쓰실 수 있어요.

phrases.en: My card isn't working.
I'm traveling in Japan.

response.situationKo: 가게에서 카드가 거절됐어요. 다른 방법으로 내겠다고 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Sorry, your card was declined.

answers.text: Oh, can you try again, please?
answers.noteKo: 다시 시도해 달라고 할 때 써요.

answers.text: That's strange. Can I pay with cash?
I'm sorry about that. Let me try another card.
Ugh, really? OK, I'll use Apple Pay.

title: Getting a SIM card
settingKo: 공항 통신사 매장에서 데이터 요금제를 고릅니다.

lines.text: Hi, I need a data plan for two weeks.
We have ten gigs for twenty dollars, or unlimited for thirty-five.
I'll take unlimited. Can I get an eSIM?
Sure. Just scan this QR code with your phone.
lines.ko: 네. 휴대폰으로 이 QR 코드만 찍으시면 돼요.

phrases.en: I need a data plan for two weeks.
Can I get an eSIM?

response.situationKo: 직원이 휴대폰 기종을 묻습니다. 대답하고 하나 더 물어보세요.
response.prompt: What phone do you have?

answers.text: I have an iPhone fifteen. Does it work with eSIM?
answers.noteKo: Does it work with ~?는 호환을 물어요.

answers.text: It's a Samsung Galaxy.
I have a Galaxy S twenty-four. Will it work here?
answers.noteKo: Will it work here?로 사용 가능한지 물어요.

answers.text: Just an old iPhone, haha. Is that OK?

title: Lunch with coworkers
settingKo: 동료가 점심을 같이 먹자고 합니다.

lines.text: Hey, a few of us are getting lunch. Want to join?
lines.ko: 우리 몇 명 점심 먹으러 가는데, 같이 갈래?

lines.text: Sure! Where are you going?
There's a new ramen place around the corner.
Sounds great. Give me five minutes to finish this email.

phrases.en: Want to join?
Give me five minutes.

response.situationKo: 동료가 점심 같이 먹자는데 오늘은 못 가요. 거절해 보세요.
response.prompt: We're going for tacos. You coming?

answers.text: Sorry, I can't today. Next time!
I brought lunch today, but thanks for asking.
Ah, I'm too busy. Can I take a rain check?
I'd love to, but I have a meeting at twelve.
answers.noteKo: I'd love to, but으로 부드럽게 거절해요.

title: My first day
settingKo: 첫 출근 날 팀장이 하루 일정을 설명합니다.

lines.text: Welcome to the team! Let me show you around.
lines.ko: 팀에 온 걸 환영해요! 회사를 안내해 줄게요.

lines.text: This morning you'll get your laptop and set up your email.
lines.ko: 오전에는 노트북을 받고 이메일을 설정할 거예요.

lines.text: Great. Is there a team meeting today?
Yes, at three. You can say hi to everyone.
lines.ko: 네, 3시에요. 다들 인사할 수 있을 거예요.

phrases.en: Let me show you around.
Is there a team meeting today?

response.situationKo: 팀 회의에서 자기소개를 해 보세요.
response.prompt: Everyone, this is our new teammate. Would you like to introduce yourself?

answers.text: Hi, I'm Min. I'm the new designer. Nice to meet you all.
Hello everyone. My name is Min, and I'm happy to be here.
answers.noteKo: happy to be here는 '함께하게 돼 기뻐요'예요.

answers.text: Hey all! I'm Min. I'll be working on the app. Excited to meet you!
answers.noteKo: I'll be working on으로 맡을 일을 말해요.

answers.text: Hi, I'm Min from Seoul. I'm excited to work with you.

title: Calling in sick
settingKo: 아파서 출근하지 못한다고 팀장에게 연락합니다.

lines.text: Hi Sarah, I'm sorry, but I can't come in today.
lines.ko: 사라, 미안한데 오늘 출근을 못 할 것 같아요.

lines.text: Oh no, are you OK?
I have a high fever. I'm going to see a doctor.
lines.ko: 열이 많이 나요. 병원에 가 보려고요.

lines.text: Take care of yourself. Don't worry about work.
lines.ko: 몸 잘 챙겨요. 일은 걱정하지 말고요.

phrases.en: I can't come in today.
phrases.ko: 오늘 출근을 못 할 것 같아요.

phrases.en: Take care of yourself.

response.situationKo: 몸이 안 좋아서 내일 쉬겠다고 팀장에게 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Hi, is everything OK? You sounded tired earlier.

answers.text: Actually, I'm not feeling well. Can I take tomorrow off?
I'm a bit sick. I think I need to rest tomorrow.
I'm sorry, I'm not feeling well. Would it be OK if I took a sick day tomorrow?
Not really. I caught a cold, so I'd like to take a day off.

title: Coffee date
settingKo: 데이팅 앱으로 만난 사람과 카페에서 처음 만납니다.

lines.text: Hi, you must be Jun. It's nice to finally meet you.
lines.ko: 안녕하세요, 준 씨죠? 드디어 만나서 반가워요.

lines.text: You too! You look just like your pictures.
Haha, thanks. So, what do you do on weekends?
lines.ko: 하하, 고마워요. 주말에는 보통 뭐 해요?

lines.text: I usually go climbing. Have you ever tried it?
lines.ko: 보통 클라이밍해요. 해 본 적 있어요?

phrases.en: It's nice to finally meet you.
Have you ever tried it?

response.situationKo: 상대가 해 본 적 있는지 묻습니다. 경험을 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Have you ever been to a music festival?

answers.text: Yes, I went to one last summer. It was amazing.
No, I haven't, but I really want to.
Never! Do you want to go together sometime?
Yes, I have, once in Seoul. Have you?
answers.noteKo: Have you?로 다시 물어 대화를 이어 가요.

title: Planning in the group chat
settingKo: 친구들과 단톡방에서 모임 날짜를 정합니다.

lines.text: Hey guys, are we still on for dinner this Friday?
lines.ko: 얘들아, 이번 금요일 저녁 아직 유효하지?

lines.text: Friday doesn't work for me anymore. How about Saturday?
lines.ko: 나 금요일 이제 안 돼. 토요일은 어때?

lines.text: Saturday works. Let's say seven at the usual place?
lines.ko: 토요일 좋아. 늘 가던 데서 7시 어때?

lines.text: Perfect. I'll book a table.

phrases.en: Are we still on for Friday?
Friday doesn't work for me.

response.situationKo: 친구가 새 날짜를 제안합니다. 되는지 안 되는지 답해 보세요.
response.prompt: Does next Sunday work for everyone?

answers.text: Sunday works for me!
Sorry, I can't on Sunday. Can we do Saturday?
answers.noteKo: 안 될 때는 대안을 같이 말해요.

answers.text: I'm in. What time?
Unfortunately, Sunday doesn't work for me. Would Monday evening be OK?

title: Any recommendations?
settingKo: 현지인 동료에게 맛집을 추천받습니다.

lines.text: Do you know any good places to eat around here?
What kind of food do you like?
Anything, but I really want to try local food.
lines.ko: 다 좋은데 현지 음식을 꼭 먹어 보고 싶어요.

lines.text: Then go to Rosa's. Their tacos are the best in town.
lines.ko: 그럼 로사네 가 봐요. 거기 타코가 동네 최고예요.

phrases.en: Do you know any good places to eat around here?
It's the best in town.

response.situationKo: 여행 온 친구가 서울 맛집을 묻습니다. 하나 추천해 보세요.
response.prompt: I'm visiting Seoul next month. Where should I eat?

answers.text: You should try Korean barbecue in Mapo.
Go to Gwangjang Market! The food is amazing.
I recommend a place called Hadongkwan. Their beef soup is famous.
My favorite is a small noodle shop near my office.

title: This isn't what I ordered
settingKo: 식당에서 주문과 다른 음식이 나왔습니다.

lines.text: Excuse me, I think this isn't what I ordered.
lines.ko: 실례합니다, 이건 제가 주문한 게 아닌 것 같아요.

lines.text: Oh, I'm sorry. What did you order?
I ordered the chicken pasta, not the beef.
My mistake. I'll bring the right one right away.
lines.ko: 제 실수예요. 바로 맞는 걸로 가져올게요.

phrases.en: This isn't what I ordered.
I'll bring the right one right away.

response.situationKo: 음식이 너무 오래 안 나와요. 직원에게 물어보세요.
response.prompt: Is everything OK here?

answers.text: We've been waiting for thirty minutes. Is our food coming?
Could you check on our order, please? It's been a while.
Our food still isn't here. How long will it be?
answers.noteKo: How long will it be?는 '얼마나 걸려요?'예요.

answers.text: Hey, any news on our pizza? We're starving!

title: Booking a yoga class
settingKo: 요가 스튜디오에 전화해서 수업을 예약합니다.

lines.text: Hi, I'd like to book a beginner class for this week.
lines.ko: 안녕하세요, 이번 주 초급 수업을 예약하고 싶어요.

lines.text: We have one on Tuesday at seven and Thursday at six.
Thursday is better. Do I need to bring a mat?
No, you can borrow one here for free.
lines.ko: 아니요, 여기서 무료로 빌릴 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I'd like to book a beginner class.
Do I need to bring a mat?

response.situationKo: 강사가 운동 경험을 묻습니다. 대답해 보세요.
response.prompt: Have you done yoga before?

answers.text: No, this is my first time.
A little, but I'm still a beginner.
Yes, I've done it a few times, but not for a while.
answers.noteKo: not for a while은 '한동안 안 했다'예요.

answers.text: Never! Please go easy on me.
answers.noteKo: go easy on me는 '살살 해 주세요'예요.

title: A little too loud
settingKo: 밤마다 시끄러운 위층 이웃에게 정중하게 말합니다.

lines.text: Hi, I live downstairs. Sorry to bother you.
lines.ko: 안녕하세요, 아래층 사는 사람이에요. 귀찮게 해서 죄송해요.

lines.text: Oh, hi. Is something wrong?
The music is a bit loud at night. I can't sleep.
lines.ko: 밤에 음악 소리가 좀 커서 잠을 못 자요.

lines.text: I'm so sorry. I'll keep it down after ten.

phrases.en: Sorry to bother you.
I'll keep it down.

response.situationKo: 이웃이 당신 강아지가 짖는다고 말합니다. 사과해 보세요.
response.prompt: Hi, um, your dog barks a lot when you're out.

answers.text: Oh, I'm so sorry. I didn't know.
I'm really sorry about that. I'll find a dog sitter.
Oh no, sorry! I'll try some training.
answers.noteKo: try some training은 '훈련을 좀 해 볼게요'예요.

answers.text: Thank you for telling me. I'll fix it.
answers.noteKo: 알려 줘서 고맙다고 하면 분위기가 부드러워요.

title: Can I borrow your charger?
settingKo: 도서관에서 옆자리 사람에게 충전기를 빌립니다.

lines.text: Sorry, can I borrow your charger for a few minutes?
lines.ko: 죄송한데, 충전기 몇 분만 빌려도 될까요?

lines.text: Sure. Is it a USB-C phone?
Yes. My battery is at two percent.
Oh, keep it as long as you need.

phrases.en: Can I borrow your charger?
Keep it as long as you need.

response.situationKo: 누군가 당신에게 펜을 빌려 달라고 합니다. 대답해 보세요.
response.prompt: Excuse me, do you have a pen I could use?

answers.text: Sure, here you go.
Of course. You can keep it.
Sorry, I don't have one.
Yeah, take this one!

title: Change of plans
settingKo: 피크닉 날 비 예보가 있어 친구와 계획을 바꿉니다.

lines.text: Did you see the weather? It's going to rain all day tomorrow.
lines.ko: 날씨 봤어? 내일 하루 종일 비 온대.

lines.text: Oh no. So no picnic in the park?
lines.ko: 이런. 그럼 공원 피크닉은 안 되겠네?

lines.text: We could go to a museum instead.
Good idea. Let's meet at the entrance at eleven.

phrases.en: It's going to rain all day.
We could go to a museum instead.

response.situationKo: 친구가 비가 오니 계획을 바꾸자고 합니다. 다른 걸 제안해 보세요.
response.prompt: It's raining. What should we do instead?

answers.text: How about a movie?
We could stay in and play board games.
Let's go to that new café instead!
Maybe we could visit the art gallery. What do you think?
answers.noteKo: What do you think?로 의견을 물어요.

title: Concert tickets
settingKo: 친구와 콘서트 티켓 예매 이야기를 합니다.

lines.text: Did you get tickets for the concert? They sold out in ten minutes!
Yes! I got two. Do you want to come with me?
lines.ko: 응! 두 장 구했어. 같이 갈래?

lines.text: Are you serious? Of course! How much do I owe you?
lines.ko: 진짜? 당연하지! 내가 얼마 주면 돼?

lines.text: Eighty dollars. Just send it whenever.

phrases.en: They sold out in ten minutes.
How much do I owe you?

response.situationKo: 친구가 남는 표가 있다며 같이 가자고 합니다. 반응해 보세요.
response.prompt: I have an extra ticket for Saturday's show. Want it?

answers.text: No way! Yes, I'd love to go.
answers.noteKo: No way!는 '말도 안 돼!' 같은 놀람이에요.

answers.text: Really? Thank you! How much was it?
That's so kind of you. I'd love to come.
Yes, please! I wanted to go so badly.

title: How was your trip?
settingKo: 동료가 다녀온 여행에 대해 묻습니다.

lines.text: Welcome back! How was Vietnam?
It was amazing. The food was so cheap and delicious.
Where did you go?
Hanoi and Da Nang. The beach in Da Nang was beautiful.
lines.ko: 하노이랑 다낭이요. 다낭 해변이 정말 예뻤어요.

phrases.en: Welcome back!
The food was so cheap and delicious.

response.situationKo: 친구가 최근 여행에 대해 묻습니다. 어땠는지 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: You went to Japan, right? How was it?

answers.text: It was great! I loved the food in Osaka.
Amazing, but it was really crowded.
It was wonderful. We went to Kyoto and saw many temples.
So good! I want to go back already.
answers.noteKo: go back already는 '벌써 또 가고 싶어'예요.

title: Helping a tourist
settingKo: 길을 묻는 관광객에게 길을 알려 줍니다.

lines.text: Excuse me, how do I get to the palace from here?
Take the subway, Line Three, and get off at Anguk.
Is it far from the station?
No, it's just five minutes from exit one.

phrases.en: How do I get to the palace?
Get off at Anguk.

response.situationKo: 관광객이 가장 가까운 편의점을 묻습니다. 알려 주세요.
response.prompt: Is there a convenience store near here?

answers.text: Yes, there's one around the corner.
Go straight and it's on your left.
Yes, it's just across the street, next to the bank.
Yep! Turn right, it's right there.

title: Picking up medicine
settingKo: 약국에서 처방약을 받고 복용법을 듣습니다.

lines.text: Hi, I'm here to pick up my prescription.
What's your name and date of birth?
Min Lee, March third, nineteen ninety-five.
Take one pill after each meal. Don't drink alcohol with it.
lines.ko: 식후에 한 알씩 드세요. 술과 함께 드시면 안 돼요.

phrases.en: I'm here to pick up my prescription.
Take one pill after each meal.

response.situationKo: 약사에게 약에 대해 하나 물어보세요.
response.prompt: Do you have any questions about this medicine?

answers.text: Will it make me sleepy?
How many times a day should I take it?
Are there any side effects I should know about?
Can I take it with coffee?

title: Hotel laundry
settingKo: 호텔 프런트에 세탁 서비스를 묻습니다.

lines.text: Hi, do you have a laundry service?
Yes. Put your clothes in the bag in your closet.
lines.ko: 네. 옷장 안 가방에 옷을 넣어 주세요.

lines.text: When will it be ready?
If you leave it before nine, you'll get it back tonight.
lines.ko: 9시 전에 맡기시면 오늘 밤에 받으실 수 있어요.

phrases.en: Do you have a laundry service?
When will it be ready?

response.situationKo: 호텔 직원이 도울 일이 있는지 묻습니다. 하나 부탁해 보세요.
response.prompt: Front desk, how may I help you?

answers.text: Could I get a wake-up call at six, please?
Hi, can I have an extra pillow?
Can I check out a bit later tomorrow?
Hey, the TV remote isn't working. Can someone bring a new one?

title: Joining an online class
settingKo: 온라인 수업 시작 전 강사와 짧게 이야기합니다.

lines.text: Hi everyone, can you all see my screen?
lines.ko: 여러분 안녕하세요, 제 화면 다 보이나요?

lines.text: Yes, I can see it. Will the class be recorded?
Yes, I'll share the recording after class.
Great, thanks. I have to leave a little early today.
lines.ko: 좋아요, 감사합니다. 오늘 조금 일찍 나가야 해서요.

phrases.en: Can you all see my screen?
Will the class be recorded?

response.situationKo: 수업 중 이해가 안 되는 부분이 있어요. 질문해 보세요.
response.prompt: OK, any questions so far?

answers.text: Could you explain the last part again?
Yes, what does 'deadline' mean?
Sorry, I didn't understand the example.
Can you go a little slower, please?

title: Language exchange
settingKo: 언어 교환 모임에서 처음 만난 사람과 이야기합니다.

lines.text: Hi! Is this your first time at the language exchange?
Yes. I want to practice speaking English.
Cool. I'm learning Korean, so we can help each other.
lines.ko: 좋아요. 저는 한국어를 배우니까 서로 도울 수 있겠네요.

lines.text: Perfect. Let's speak English first, then Korean.
lines.ko: 좋아요. 영어 먼저 하고, 그다음에 한국어로 해요.

phrases.en: I want to practice speaking English.
We can help each other.

response.situationKo: 상대가 영어를 왜 배우는지 묻습니다. 이유를 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: So why are you learning English?

answers.text: For my job. I have meetings in English.
Because I want to travel and make friends.
I'd like to work abroad someday, so I'm practicing hard.
Honestly, I just want to watch Netflix without subtitles!

title: Looking for a gift
settingKo: 가게 직원에게 엄마 생신 선물을 추천받습니다.

lines.text: Hi there. Are you looking for anything special?
Yes, a birthday gift for my mom. She loves gardening.
lines.ko: 네, 엄마 생신 선물이요. 정원 가꾸기를 좋아하세요.

lines.text: How about these gloves? They're our best seller.
lines.ko: 이 장갑 어떠세요? 제일 잘 팔리는 거예요.

lines.text: They're nice. Could you gift wrap them, please?
lines.ko: 좋네요. 선물 포장 해 주실 수 있나요?

phrases.en: I'm looking for a birthday gift for my mom.
Could you gift wrap it?
phrases.ko: 선물 포장 해 주실 수 있나요?

response.situationKo: 직원이 예산을 묻습니다. 대답해 보세요.
response.prompt: What's your budget?

answers.text: Around fifty dollars.
Under a hundred, if possible.
Not more than thirty dollars, please.
Honestly, up to forty bucks.

title: Cooking together
settingKo: 친구 집에서 같이 파스타를 만듭니다.

lines.text: Can you cut the onions while I boil the water?
lines.ko: 내가 물 끓이는 동안 양파 좀 썰어 줄래?

lines.text: Sure. How small should I cut them?
Really small, please. My kids don't like big pieces.
lines.ko: 아주 작게. 우리 애들이 큰 건 싫어해.

lines.text: Got it. Do you have another knife?

phrases.en: Can you cut the onions?
How small should I cut them?

response.situationKo: 친구가 요리를 도와 달라고 합니다. 할 일을 물어보세요.
response.prompt: Dinner is in thirty minutes. Can you help me?

answers.text: Sure! What can I do?
Of course. Should I wash the vegetables?
Yeah, I can set the table.
Sure, but I'm not a good cook, haha.

title: I left my bag in the car
settingKo: 앱으로 탄 차에 가방을 두고 내려 기사에게 연락합니다.

lines.text: Hi, you just drove me to the airport. I think I left my bag in your car.
lines.ko: 안녕하세요, 방금 공항까지 태워 주셨는데요. 차에 가방을 두고 내린 것 같아요.

lines.text: Let me check. Is it a small black backpack?
Yes, that's it! Can you bring it back?
lines.ko: 네, 그거예요! 다시 가져다주실 수 있나요?

lines.text: Sure, I'll be back at gate three in ten minutes.

phrases.en: I think I left my bag in your car.
phrases.ko: 차에 가방을 두고 내린 것 같아요.

phrases.en: Can you bring it back?

response.situationKo: 기사님이 가방을 가져다주셨어요. 고마움을 표현해 보세요.
response.prompt: Here's your bag. Have a safe flight!

answers.text: Thank you so much! You're a lifesaver.
Thank you. I really appreciate it.
Thanks a lot! Can I give you a tip?
Oh, thank you! I was so worried.

title: Going hiking
settingKo: 주말 등산 계획을 친구와 세웁니다.

lines.text: Do you want to go hiking on Sunday morning?
Sure, but not a hard trail. I'm out of shape.
lines.ko: 좋아, 근데 힘든 코스는 말고. 나 체력이 안 좋아.

lines.text: There's an easy one. It takes about two hours.
OK. I'll bring snacks and water.

phrases.en: I'm out of shape.
It takes about two hours.

response.situationKo: 친구가 등산할 때 무엇을 가져가야 하는지 묻습니다.
response.prompt: What should I bring for the hike?

answers.text: Bring water and comfortable shoes.
You should bring a jacket. It gets cold at the top.
Just snacks and good shoes!
Water, sunscreen, and a hat.

title: Did you like the movie?
settingKo: 영화를 보고 나와서 친구와 소감을 나눕니다.

lines.text: So, what did you think of the movie?
I loved it, but the ending was a little sad.
lines.ko: 너무 좋았어. 근데 결말이 좀 슬펐어.

lines.text: Really? I thought the ending was perfect.
Maybe. The music was amazing, though.
lines.ko: 그럴 수도. 그래도 음악은 정말 좋았어.

gist.questionKo: 두 사람이 모두 좋다고 한 것은?

phrases.en: What did you think of the movie?
The ending was a little sad.

response.situationKo: 친구가 최근에 본 드라마를 추천해 달라고 합니다.
response.prompt: Have you watched anything good lately?

answers.text: Yes, I watched a great Korean drama. You should try it.
Check out the new season of my favorite show. It's so good!
I recently watched a documentary about the ocean. It was really interesting.
Yes! It's about a chef in Paris. Really good.

title: Can you watch my cat?
settingKo: 여행 가는 동안 이웃에게 고양이를 부탁합니다.

lines.text: I'm going away this weekend. Could you feed my cat?
lines.ko: 이번 주말에 어디 가는데, 고양이 밥 좀 줄 수 있어?

lines.text: Of course. How often does she eat?
Twice a day, morning and evening. The food is in the kitchen.
lines.ko: 하루 두 번, 아침이랑 저녁. 사료는 부엌에 있어.

lines.text: No problem. Just leave me your key.

phrases.en: Could you feed my cat?
phrases.ko: 고양이 밥 좀 줄 수 있어?

phrases.en: How often does she eat?

response.situationKo: 친구가 집을 비우는 동안 화분에 물을 줘 달라고 합니다.
response.prompt: Could you water my plants while I'm away?

answers.text: Sure. How often should I water them?
Of course, I'd be happy to.
No problem! Just text me the details.
Sure, but I'm away on Sunday. Is that OK?

title: New year goals
settingKo: 친구와 새해 목표를 이야기합니다.

lines.text: Do you have any goals for this year?
I want to read one book a month and spend less time on my phone.
lines.ko: 한 달에 책 한 권 읽고 휴대폰 보는 시간을 줄이고 싶어.

lines.text: Good luck with the phone one. That's hard!
I know. I already deleted TikTok.

gist.questionKo: 두 번째 사람이 이미 한 일은?

phrases.en: Do you have any goals for this year?
I want to spend less time on my phone.

response.situationKo: 친구가 올해 목표를 묻습니다. 하나 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: What's one thing you want to do this year?

answers.text: I want to learn how to swim.
My goal is to save money for a trip.
I'd like to get better at English, so I'm practicing every day.
answers.noteKo: get better at은 '~를 더 잘하게 되다'예요.

answers.text: Honestly? Sleep more. I'm always tired.

title: My laptop won't turn on
settingKo: 회사 노트북이 켜지지 않아 IT팀에 연락합니다.

lines.text: Hi, my laptop won't turn on. I have a meeting in an hour.
lines.ko: 안녕하세요, 노트북이 안 켜져요. 한 시간 뒤에 회의가 있어요.

lines.text: Did you try charging it?
Yes, it's plugged in, but nothing happens.
lines.ko: 네, 꽂혀 있는데 아무 반응이 없어요.

lines.text: Bring it to the fourth floor. I'll give you a spare one.

phrases.en: My laptop won't turn on.
Nothing happens.

response.situationKo: IT 담당자가 어떤 문제인지 묻습니다. 설명해 보세요.
response.prompt: Hi, what's the issue?

answers.text: My email isn't working. I can't send anything.
The Wi-Fi keeps disconnecting.
I'm sorry to bother you, but I can't log in to my account.
My screen is frozen and I get an error message.

title: Farewell party
settingKo: 회사를 떠나는 동료의 송별회에서 인사합니다.

lines.text: I can't believe it's your last day!
I know. I'm going to miss working with you.
lines.ko: 그러게요. 같이 일하던 게 그리울 거예요.

lines.text: Let's keep in touch. Good luck at your new job!
lines.ko: 연락하고 지내요. 새 직장에서 잘되길 바라요!

lines.text: Thanks. Let's grab dinner next month.
lines.ko: 고마워요. 다음 달에 저녁 같이 먹어요.

gist.questionKo: 두 사람은 다음 달에 무엇을 하기로 했나요?

phrases.en: Let's keep in touch.
I'm going to miss working with you.

response.situationKo: 떠나는 동료에게 작별 인사를 해 보세요.
response.prompt: Well, this is goodbye for now!

answers.text: Good luck! Let's keep in touch.
answers.noteKo: 작별할 때 가장 흔한 두 표현이에요.

answers.text: I'll miss you! Take care.
Thank you for everything. I learned so much from you.
answers.noteKo: learned so much from you는 진심이 담긴 인사예요.

answers.text: Good luck with everything. Don't forget us!
answers.noteKo: Don't forget us는 가벼운 농담처럼 써요.
